messages:
support-ops: getting a small but persistent set of p99 latency complaints for /v1/generate in us-west since ~15:20 PDT. 3 customers reporting timeouts, support ticket IDs linked in the dashboard.
eli-oncall: thanks — which model and plan? any error codes from clients?
support-ops: mostly redwood-tiny-v1 on hosted, standard plan. clients see 504s and very long durations (2000-4000ms p99). nothing obvious in auth or billing.
maya-sre: hmm, dashboard shows increased queue length on gw-proxy-usw and increased CPU on serving-pool-usw-a. p95 is ok, p99 drifting. could be noisy tail from >seq len or batching bug.
samir-runtime: I can check KV cache hit rates + recent kernel rollouts. rolling change to kernel-ops happened at 15:05 but rollout was gradual.
eli-oncall: while you check, put immediate mitigations: 1) enable circuit breaker for this route to degrade to v1-small fallback (lower mem) 2) tighten concurrency for standard plan to protect infra 3) route burst traffic to eu-west as fallback policy if latency > 800ms for 30s.
julia-product: we need to avoid model-quality regressions for customers — fallback must be clearly labeled and opt-in for critical accounts.
maya-sre: doing 1 & 2 now. applying temporary route override to send 20% traffic to v1-small and 80% to v1-tiny to reduce mem pressure. also setting cb tripping threshold: p99 > 1200ms for 60s.
samir-runtime: checking cache metrics: prefix cache hit rate dropped from 86% -> 41% after 15:10. looks like cache invalidation churn — likely due to new prefix-split change.
eli-oncall: can we hotfix cache config? quick fix: increase cache TTL and disable aggressive invalidation to recover hit rate.
samir-runtime: increasing TTL from 30s -> 5m on serving-pool-usw (hotpatch). watching.
infra-bot: rollback job queued: kernel-ops-2026-03-17-1505 -> can rollback to kernel-ops-2026-03-10-1402. confirm to continue.
maya-sre: hold on rollback until we see KV hit recovery. rollback has risk; prefer caching and throttles first.
eli-oncall: also add a rate-limit exception for internal admin routes and throttle lower-priority customer routes to 20 rps per customer for 10m. publish banner in status page.
support-ops: posted banner and tied tickets to mitigation. customers notified: regressions acknowledged, mitigation in progress.
10m-later
samir-runtime: KV cache hit rate recovered to 79%, serving-pool CPU trending down. p99 reduced from ~2200ms -> ~950ms.
maya-sre: circuit breaker hasn't tripped anymore. routing override lowered queue. leaving CB in place for 30m, then we can incrementally relax.
julia-product: prepare an email draft for affected customers explaining fallback behavior and next steps; include explicit SLA remediation options.
eli-oncall: follow-up actions: - create a post-incident issue for prefix-split rollout to add canary traffic and observability for cache churn - add a guardrail: if cache hit rate drops >30% relative to baseline, auto-scale cache size or pause rollout - add model-fallback policy that requires a label explaining quality delta - improve per-route p99 alert to include correlated queue length and cache hit rate.
support-ops: noted. I've attached repro steps from one customer: payload with many long context messages (avg seq_len 3.2k) that triggered large KV growth. reproducible locally with: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-tiny-v1","input":"<very long chat...>"}'
```
eli-oncall: add a quota cap on sequence length for standard plan (max 2048 tokens) to protect infra, and route oversize requests to a special high-memory queue on Dedicated customers only.
maya-sre: I've drafted the playbook update: short checklist, commands to flip circuit breaker, route override, cache TTL patch, and rollback decision tree. will add to runbook repo.
samir-runtime: monitoring note: add synthetic traffic with long contexts in canary to surface KV churn before full rollout.
eli-oncall: good. I'll keep CB and throttles for 30m more, then will schedule a slow rollback of prefix-split if metrics don't stabilize. thanks team :thumbsup:
